About Me

I am an undergraduate student in Computer Science and Technology at Hangzhou Dianzi University and ITMO University. My research interests center on natural language processing (NLP), large language models (LLMs), and AI agents. I am particularly interested in multi-agent collaboration, reliable reasoning, and efficient representations for systems that understand tasks, use tools, and interact with their environments.

My work involves zero-shot object navigation, neuro-symbolic multi-agent systems and controllable data synthesis, and model performance evaluation with few labels. I am also interested in KV cache compression, inference acceleration, long-context processing, and latent-space representation and reasoning, aiming to improve reasoning efficiency, reliability, and generalization under limited compute and memory budgets. In addition, I actively explore applications of LLMs and agent systems in embodied intelligence and AI for Science.

I am also active in competitive programming and received an ICPC Asia Regional silver medal. I have served as a problem setter for the Guangxi Collegiate Programming Contest (GXCPC), the Inner Mongolia Collegiate Programming Contest (NMCPC), and the Hangzhou Dianzi University Multi-University Training Contest, among other contests.

Research Interests

  • Large Language Models & Multi-agent Systems: NLP, LLMs, agents, task planning and tool use, multi-agent collaboration, memory and reflection, neuro-symbolic reasoning, controllable data synthesis.
  • Latent Space & Efficient Inference: latent-space representation and reasoning, compact semantic representations, KV cache compression, inference acceleration, long-context processing, parameter-efficient adaptation.
  • AI for Science & Trustworthy Evaluation: scientific data synthesis, evidence-grounded reasoning, few-label performance prediction, uncertainty-aware evaluation.
